faqs.q: The whole of the Indian subcontinent came to be known by which name after an ancient tribe called the Bharatas?
The descendants of the Bharata tribe, from whom the ancients viewed the country as one unit, were called by which term?

Kings who tried to establish their authority from the Himalayas to Cape Comorin and from the Brahmaputra to the Indus were called:
Consider the following pairs:

(I) Asoka – third century B.C. (II) Samudragupta – fourth century A.D. (III) Pulakesin II – seventh century (Chalukya)
Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched with the century in which they extended their sway over most of the country?
faqs.e: Asoka extended his empire over most of the country in the third century B.C.; Samudragupta carried his victorious arms up to the Tamil borders in the fourth century A.D.; and the Chalukya king Pulakesin II subjugated Harshavardhana in the seventh century.

faqs.q: Which language served as the lingua franca of the country in the third century B.C.?
In which period did Sanskrit become prominent as the state language even in the remotest parts of the country?
The word "Hind" is derived from which Sanskrit term?
faqs.e: The country came to be known as "India" in Greek and "Hind" in Persian and Arabic, both derived from the Sanskrit term Sindhu.

faqs.e: Prinsep was a civil servant employed by the East India Company in Bengal; an earlier Asokan pillar inscription brought to Delhi by Firoz Shah Tughlaq had failed to be deciphered by his court pandits.

The Mahabharata was originally called Jaya Samhita, dealing with:
faqs.e: It originally had 8800 verses, later raised to 24000 as Bharata, and finally to 100,000 verses known as the Mahabharata or Satasahasri Samhita.

faqs.q: The Ramayana originally consisted of 12000 verses, which were later raised to:
The Dharmasutras and Smritis, together with their commentaries called Dharmasastras, were compiled in which period?
The Arthasastra, an important law-book on polity and economy, was authored by:
faqs.e: Its text is divided into fifteen books, of which Books II and III may be of an earlier date; it was given final form in the beginning of the Christian era.

faqs.e:
Megasthenes came to the court of Chandragupta Maurya and mentioned Sandrokottas, a contemporary of Alexander, identified with Chandragupta.

faqs.q: From the early centuries of the Christian era, India developed intimate connections with Burma and which peninsula, which possessed plenty of tin, enabling large-scale use of bronze in south India?

faqs.e: Silver mines existed in early times in the Kharagpur hills in the district of Monghyr, accounting for the use of this white metal in the earliest punch-marked coins found in Bihar.
